personas.background: Matriarch of the Okonkwo family, originally from Enugu state and now living in Reading. Ran a school for 22 years before retiring. Firmly holds the family together — organises reunions, coordinates logistics, and is the emotional anchor for disputes. Has strong opinions on how family events should be run and does not soften them.

food.value: insists on cooking ofe onugbu and jollof rice for any family gathering of more than four people — becomes visibly offended if someone orders takeaway instead

activities.value: prefers in-person visits to phone or video calls — will explicitly say 'you should come and see me' rather than arrange a call

social.value: dislikes WhatsApp voice messages — always replies with text even when sent a voice note

domain_specific.value: expects full family attendance at Christmas and Easter — treats partial attendance as a personal slight

preference_history.old_value: resistant to video calls — prefers in-person contact and has declined many family Zoom sessions
preference_history.new_value: accepts regular video calls as a genuine substitute when travel is not possible, initiated by herself during a health episode
preference_history.trigger: had a minor health scare and could not travel for three weeks; the family set up a weekly Sunday video call and she found she looked forward to it

speaking_quirks: opens messages with 'My children,' regardless of whether she is addressing one person or seven
appends 'God willing' or 'by His grace' to any future plan
uses rhetorical questions when displeased ('And nobody thought to call me first?')

personas.background: Eldest of Nkechi's children. Lives in Leeds with his wife and two young children. High-pressure career means he is frequently the least available family member but tries to compensate by being decisive about logistics when he does engage. Has a habit of reframing family discussions in terms of 'what we actually need to decide here.'

food.value: maintains a strict low-fat diet and avoids heavy fried food — never mentions it but consistently declines those dishes at family meals

activities.value: runs every morning regardless of location — has declined family breakfast plans that start before 9am because of his run

social.value: prefers to communicate in the group only for decisions — does not engage in chat threads that are purely social

domain_specific.value: reluctant to take on family financial coordination — defers to Adaeze even when asked directly

preference_history.old_value: attends family events only at Christmas and summer — declines all other gatherings citing work schedule
preference_history.new_value: has committed to attending at least one additional family event per quarter after his children started asking why they never saw their cousins
preference_history.trigger: his daughter asked at dinner why the cousins from London 'never come here' — he mentioned it in the chat the following week and Nkechi immediately locked him in

speaking_quirks: asks 'what's the actual decision point here?' when threads go on too long
responds to emotional messages with a single practical offer ('let me know if you need anything sorted')
signs off with 'E' rather than his name

personas.occupation: Chartered accountant and part-time finance lecturer
personas.background: Second of Nkechi's children, lives in London. Manages the family's shared financial arrangements — the Christmas fund, the Mum's-birthday pot, and any joint purchases. Everyone assumes she enjoys this role but she has quietly found it exhausting for two years. Very close to her brother Emeka but occasionally frustrated by his tendency to disengage.

food.value: always brings chin chin or puff puff to family events — her contribution is so reliable it is never discussed

activities.value: attends a Afrobeats dance class on Thursday evenings that she refuses to cancel for any reason short of emergency

social.value: prefers to sort logistics in private DMs rather than the group chat to avoid public disagreements

domain_specific.value: growing reluctance to manage the Christmas fund alone — has hinted several times that she needs a co-administrator but no one has picked it up

preference_history.old_value: happily manages all family financial coordination — treats it as her contribution
preference_history.new_value: openly asking for help with the Christmas fund management after two consecutive years of running it solo through stressful periods
preference_history.trigger: sent a message in session 6 saying 'I love doing this but I genuinely need someone to share this with me this year — I nearly dropped it in November'

speaking_quirks: uses 'okay so' to open any message that is about to deliver news or a decision
follows up every group announcement with a numbered list if there are more than two action items
adds '(no stress!)' after requests to soften the ask

personas.occupation: Software engineer at a fintech startup
personas.background: Third child of Nkechi, the quietest of the siblings. Lives in Manchester. Works long hours in a fast-moving startup and finds family group dynamics slightly overwhelming — tends to lurk and react rather than initiate. Closest to his younger sister Chisom and occasionally protective of her in the family chat.

food.value: dislikes cooking but always offers to handle drinks and snacks — shows up with a specific set of drinks nobody asked for but everyone appreciates

activities.value: watches football every weekend without exception — has declined Sunday family calls that clash with a match without apology

social.value: almost never initiates conversations in the group — responds to others or reacts with emojis, rarely adds new threads

domain_specific.value: finds big group gatherings draining — tends to disappear to a quieter room at family events after about two hours

preference_history.old_value: spends most free evenings gaming alone — does not engage with the family group outside of reply obligations
preference_history.new_value: started a family FIFA tournament chat subgroup with Chisom and two cousins — shows noticeably more spontaneous engagement
preference_history.trigger: Chisom challenged him to a FIFA match over video call during lockdown boredom and it became a regular thing; he built it into a proper bracket

speaking_quirks: responds to long messages with a single emoji and a one-line reply
uses 'tbf' (to be fair) before any concession
types in all lowercase without punctuation most of the time

personas.background: Youngest of Nkechi's children, currently rotating through hospital placements in Birmingham. High-energy and emotionally expressive — the most vocal in the chat by message count. She overshares her shift experiences and invites the family into her emotional state in real time. Close to Tobenna and less close to Emeka, whom she finds hard to read.

skills_list.skill: cooking jollof rice and Nigerian street food

food.value: lives off hospital canteen food and deliveroo during placements — is excited by any homemade food without being selective

activities.value: loves surprise plans and last-minute spontaneity — often the one to say 'let's just go!' without consulting her schedule

social.value: sends voice messages exclusively when tired or emotional — switches to text only for calm practical exchanges

domain_specific.value: deeply uncomfortable when family conflict stays unresolved — will push for a resolution conversation even when others want to leave it alone

preference_history.old_value: planning to pursue surgery after foundation years — has told the whole family this multiple times
preference_history.new_value: now considering psychiatry after a rotation she found unexpectedly meaningful
preference_history.trigger: completed a psychiatry rotation in session 7's timeframe and came back to the family chat describing it as 'the first time I felt like I was actually helping not just fixing' — mentioned she might change her plan

speaking_quirks: starts dramatic updates with 'okay SO' in all caps
uses 'I can't' as an expression of strong emotion ('I actually can't with this shift')
double-messages constantly — sends a thought, then immediately sends a follow-up correction or addition

personas.occupation: Retired civil servant (former Ministry of Works, Nigeria)
personas.background: Nkechi's older sister, based in Enugu but visits the UK twice a year. Known in the family as 'Aunty Oby'. The most traditional member of the group — her messages carry the weight of family custom. Frequently the one to invoke extended-family expectations and the first to reference what 'the family has always done.' Not always agreed with, but always heard.

food.value: eats only traditional Igbo food at family gatherings — politely but visibly declines anything she considers 'oyinbo food'

activities.value: expects formal acknowledgement of elders at the start of any family gathering — has corrected her nieces and nephews when they skipped this

social.value: does not use voice messages or video calls — prefers written text and expects proper sentences with greetings

domain_specific.value: strongly opposed to Christmas gatherings that include non-family guests — believes family time should be uncontaminated by outsiders

preference_history.old_value: flatly refuses to attend any family event that includes non-family guests — has declined two gatherings on this basis
preference_history.new_value: will tolerate non-family guests if they are partners of family members, following Emeka's wife attending Christmas
preference_history.trigger: Emeka's wife Funmi was present at the Christmas gathering Aunty Oby attended; she observed the dynamic for a full day before conceding privately to Nkechi that 'Funmi is practically family now'

speaking_quirks: opens messages with a formal salutation ('Greetings my people,') before any content
invokes family precedent by name ('As your grandfather used to say...' or 'In our family, we have always...')
never uses abbreviations — writes out full words including 'WhatsApp' in full

personas.background: Nkechi's nephew through her late husband's side — his father and Nkechi's husband were brothers. Based in South East London. Loud, generative, and commercially minded. Constantly proposing ideas for family ventures — a family Airbnb property, a reunion in Lagos, a family investment pool. Most ideas land with varying enthusiasm. He is the family's optimist and occasionally its irritant.

food.value: always offers to 'handle the meat' at any family barbecue — takes over the grill regardless of whether he was asked

activities.value: pushes for Lagos or Enugu as the reunion destination every year — enthusiastic about showing the next generation Nigeria but has not been in three years himself

social.value: uses the group chat to pitch ideas before he has thought them through — drops half-formed proposals and expects others to build on them

domain_specific.value: strongly resists being the one to plan logistics — generates ideas but consistently redirects execution to Adaeze or Nkechi

preference_history.old_value: enthusiastically pitches family reunion plans but drops out of the planning process once others are invested
preference_history.new_value: followed through on one planning task for the first time — booked venue deposits for the summer gathering after Adaeze called him out publicly
preference_history.trigger: Adaeze sent a message saying 'Kingsley, you proposed this one — you book the venue this time, I'll do everything else.' He went quiet for two days then sent a booking confirmation.

speaking_quirks: opens proposals with 'hear me out' regardless of how straightforward the idea is
uses 'on God' to signal that he is being serious for once
responds to practical objections with 'details, details' and pivots to the bigger picture

personas.background: Kingsley's younger sister, also on the extended Okonkwo side. Lives in Bristol. Thoughtful, socially careful, and frequently the voice of moderation when Kingsley or Nkechi escalate. Often the one to send a quiet DM to the person who just got called out. Has a deep interest in the family's history and cultural heritage that she shares tactfully — never lecturing, always offering.

food.value: pescatarian — announces it once when joining any shared meal planning discussion and does not bring it up again unless directly asked

activities.value: strongly prefers structured family activities over unstructured gatherings — suggests games, storytelling rounds, or cooking projects to give events a spine

social.value: sends individual check-in messages after difficult family threads — always checks in privately with whoever was called out or upset

domain_specific.value: quietly working on a family history project — photographs old documents and asks elders gentle questions about the past without making it a group announcement

preference_history.old_value: keeps family history interest private — does not share findings in the group for fear of being seen as lecturing
preference_history.new_value: began sharing occasional photos of old family documents and brief captions in the group after Aunty Oby explicitly encouraged her in session 6
preference_history.trigger: Aunty Oby said in the chat 'Ifeoma, show them what you showed me — these children do not know where they come from.' Ifeoma posted three archive photos that same evening.

speaking_quirks: begins gentle corrections with 'I think what might help here is...'
signs off emotionally supportive messages with a single 'x' (no other punctuation)
uses 'worth noting' before any observation she expects to be overlooked

edges.history_summary: Nkechi is enormously proud of Emeka and his career but finds his detachment from the family emotionally hurtful. She has learned to read his brevity as love but occasionally calls him out in the chat. He sends her a private voice note every Sunday, which the rest of the family does not know about.
shared_events: first family Christmas after the father's death

edges.history_summary: The most consistently functional parent-child pairing in the family. Adaeze is Nkechi's logistical right hand and they speak multiple times a week. Nkechi praises Adaeze publicly and frequently. The only real friction is around Adaeze's unspoken exhaustion with family coordination duties.
shared_events: coordinating the family's Christmas fund for six consecutive years

edges.history_summary: Nkechi finds Tobenna hard to read and occasionally wonders if he is unhappy. He is consistent at Christmas and calls on birthdays but does not volunteer personal information. She has asked Adaeze whether something is wrong with him more than once.

Nkechi dotes on Chisom in a way she is less guarded about than with her older children. Chisom rings her mother most frequently of all the siblings and Nkechi responds with lengthy advice that Chisom rarely follows but always receives warmly.

Nkechi and Obiageli have the warmth of a lifelong sisterhood and the friction of two strong-willed women who have occasionally disagreed sharply on how to raise children and manage family money. They speak candidly to each other in ways they cannot with anyone else. Obiageli's traditionalism and Nkechi's pragmatism create recurring low-level tension.
shared_events: care of their mother in her final years

edges.history_summary: Nkechi has been fond of Kingsley since he was a teenager. She indulges his big talk more than her own children do. But she has told Adaeze privately that she wishes he would follow through more. She backs him publicly and gives him quiet corrections in private.
shared_events: Kingsley's first property project where Nkechi gave character advice

edges.history_summary: Nkechi has a quiet respect for Ifeoma's steadiness and her interest in the family's history. They share a sensibility around cultural preservation even if Nkechi is too busy to pursue it actively. She has been generous with Ifeoma during difficult periods.
shared_events: Ifeoma's visit to Reading for family history research
shared conversations about the late Mr Okonkwo

edges.history_summary: The most functional sibling pairing. Emeka trusts Adaeze's judgement completely on financial matters. They have a running thread where they coordinate family logistics away from the main group. Occasionally Adaeze finds his bluntness too much when directed at the younger ones.
shared_events: joint management of family finances post-father's death

edges.history_summary: Chisom has always found Emeka slightly intimidating. He is supportive of her career in an abstract way but their communication is sparse. He acknowledged her FY2 progress with a brief 'well done, keep it up' which she told Tobenna was 'typical Emeka.'
shared_events: one joint video call during a family health scare

edges.history_summary: Adaeze checks in on Tobenna more than anyone else. She is the family member who noticed he was withdrawn and raised it with Emeka. Tobenna appreciates her without being demonstrative about it.

edges.relationship_type: protective older brother and younger sister
edges.history_summary: The tightest sibling bond in the group. Tobenna is one of very few people Chisom does not overshare with — she tells him only what she wants to, which he seems to understand intuitively. He backed her when she was criticised in the group chat for cancelling Christmas at short notice.
shared_events: Tobenna defending Chisom in the Christmas cancellation thread

edges.history_summary: Obiageli approved of Ifeoma's interest in family history from the start and has been a source for the project. She views Ifeoma as the kind of young person who carries culture forward correctly. This is one of the few relationships where Obiageli does not resort to instruction.
shared_events: sessions where Obiageli shared oral history with Ifeoma
Ifeoma's archive photo posts in the chat

edges.history_summary: They are close but frequently frustrated with each other. Kingsley finds Ifeoma overly cautious and she finds him all talk. She was the one who suggested Adaeze call him out over the venue booking. He is still slightly cool about that.
shared_events: multiple family gatherings in the UK

edges.relationship_type: aunt and niece — sometimes at odds
edges.history_summary: Obiageli disapproves of what she sees as Adaeze doing everything herself without demanding proper family participation — she has said directly that Adaeze 'enables laziness.' Adaeze finds Aunty Oby's traditionalism exhausting when it manifests as criticism. They are respectful but there is real friction.
shared_events: public disagreement over the Christmas fund approach
Aunty Oby's comments about Adaeze 'not delegating properly'

edges.history_summary: Emeka is polite and correct with Aunty Oby. He respects her seniority but has never sought her counsel or engaged with her traditionalism. She privately considers him too Westernised. They coexist comfortably at a distance.

Kingsley and Chisom bring similar energy to the group chat and frequently riff off each other. She hypes his ideas and he enthusiastically supports her updates. Neither takes the other very seriously but both enjoy the dynamic.
shared_events: joint hype threads in the family chat
one summer gathering where they planned the entertainment together

edges.relationship_type: quiet one and loud one — tolerated distance
edges.history_summary: Tobenna and Kingsley have little in common. Tobenna finds Kingsley's noise level grating in a group context. Kingsley does not notice. They are perfectly pleasant at gatherings but do not seek each other out.
shared_events: the FIFA group chat Tobenna created (Kingsley is a member but never plays)

group_norms.norm_text: Family news — jobs, relationships, health — gets announced in the group first before going to social media
Everyone contributes to the Christmas fund by 1 December each year
When Mum cooks for a gathering, you eat what she makes — no requesting alternatives
We greet elders first when entering any family gathering before greeting peers
